steps.title: Prepare 70% ethanol cleaning solution
steps.instruction: Mix 350 mL of 200‑proof pure ethanol (Koptec catalog 89125‑172) with 150 mL de‑ionized water to obtain 500 mL of 70 % ethanol; place the solution in a 500 mL spray bottle (VWR catalog 10216‑884) and keep paper towels (Georgia‑Pacific catalog B0017TKE8G) nearby for cleaning.

steps.title: Set up arena lighting and camera
steps.instruction: Ensure the testing arena is non‑reflective (e.g., line with matte white paper). Turn on the appropriate illumination source for the time of day (visible light or infrared), adjust angle/brightness, connect the camera, and focus the lens until a clear image is obtained. Verify that lighting and camera are ready before bringing mice into the testing room.

steps.title: Select and house experimental mice
steps.instruction: Use adult (4‑month‑old) wild‑type C57BL/6J mice (Jax #000664), both sexes, born and raised in the laboratory colony. Transport mice in their home cage to the behavioral testing room and have a clean holding cage ready to temporarily house each tested mouse.

steps.title: Day 1 – Habituation (open‑field recording)
steps.instruction: Acclimate mice in their home cage for 1 hour after arrival. For each mouse, place it in the centre of the empty arena facing the north wall, start video recording, and allow exploration for 5 minutes (recording optional). After recording, move the mouse to the clean holding cage, then spray the arena with 70 % ethanol, wipe with paper towels, and let air‑dry for 2–3 minutes before testing the next mouse. Once all mice are tested, return them to their home cage and then to the vivarium.

steps.title: Day 2 – Familiarization with identical objects
steps.instruction: Repeat the lighting and camera setup and allow a 1‑hour acclimation as on Day 1. Place two identical objects on opposite sides of the arena, each at least 5 cm from the arena walls. For each mouse, place it in the arena centre facing away from the objects, record video, and allow exploration for 10 minutes. After recording, move the mouse to the clean holding cage, then clean the arena and both objects with 70 % ethanol, wipe with paper towels, and air‑dry for 2–3 minutes before the next mouse. After all mice are tested, return them to their home cage and vivarium.

steps.title: Pause point – interval before test
steps.instruction: The interval between the familiarization session (Day 2) and the test session (Day 3) can be 10–15 minutes for short‑term memory assessment or 24 hours or longer for long‑term and time‑of‑day‑dependent learning experiments, depending on experimental design.

steps.title: Day 3 – Test with novel object
steps.instruction: Perform lighting and camera setup and allow a 1‑hour acclimation as before. Replace one of the two familiar objects with a novel object, positioning it in the same location as the removed object and keeping ≥5 cm from arena walls. For each mouse, place it in the arena centre facing away from the objects, record video, and allow exploration for 10 minutes. After recording, move the mouse to the clean holding cage, then clean the arena and both objects with 70 % ethanol, wipe with paper towels, and let air‑dry for 2–3 minutes before testing the next mouse. After all mice are tested, return them to the vivarium.

steps.title: Collect tissue or euthanize after test
steps.instruction: Twenty‑four hours after the final behavioral session, collect brain tissue for downstream processing or euthanize the mice, ensuring that tissue collection occurs at the same time of day as the behavior.
